summary: Open-source month: two GitHub round-ups (agent org charts, memory, voice cloning, design skills, Claude Code templates; then nine self-hosted business tools) plus agent-with-humans tools (GrokBot, Meta Muse, Hyperagent, Dots). Impeccable, Claude Code Templates and Paperclip are most useful for Charlie.

tools.name: Paperclip
tools.what: Open-source platform that gives AI agents an org chart, tasks and permissions so they work together.
tools.shown: Hosts walked through the repo and its permissions; no full build.
tools.quote: your agents get an org chart to work together

tools.name: Hindsight
tools.what: Persistent AI memory so an agent remembers you across sessions; built by a real company.
tools.shown: Discussed on the repo page; hosts unsure why it took off.
tools.quote: remembers you across your sessions
tools.check: Star count may be inflated; unverified.

tools.name: VoiceStudio
tools.what: Free local voice cloning with Mac, Windows and Linux apps, instead of a hosted service.
tools.shown: Showed the repo and the easy-install apps; no clone demo.
tools.quote: This is for people who want to clone their voices, but not pay a service like 11 Labs to host it.

tools.name: AI Engineering From Scratch
tools.what: Free step-by-step AI engineering course.
tools.shown: Looked at the repo; hosts doubted its quality (AI-written, verbose).
tools.quote: This is a free course

tools.name: Anthropic Financial Services
tools.what: Anthropic plugin of about 10 skill files that make an agent act like a finance professional.
tools.shown: Hosts discussed it; said it is for financial professionals.
tools.quote: I think it's just 10 skill files

tools.name: Next.js
tools.what: Popular JavaScript web framework; trending after a run of security fixes.
tools.shown: Explained what it is and why the fixes matter.
tools.quote: They had eight security fixes in eight days

tools.name: Impeccable
tools.what: Skill pack that gives a coding agent a designer's eye so apps stop looking generic.
tools.shown: Demoed picking an aesthetic and pasting the prompt into an agent.
tools.quote: give your coding agent a designer's eye

tools.name: CLI-Anything
tools.what: Turns desktop apps into command-line interfaces that agents can drive; small marketplace of ready-made ones.
tools.shown: Explained with a booking example; noted it does not cover Uber.
tools.quote: turn any app into a command line, your agent can drive

tools.name: Claude Skills
tools.what: Repo of 388 job-specific skill playbooks and personas.
tools.shown: Showed the repo; hosts joked about too many skills.
tools.quote: Your AI assistant is going to get 388 job-specific playbooks
tools.check: Downloaded skills need checking before install (the show warns about plugins).

tools.name: Claude Code Templates
tools.what: One-command install of skills, commands and settings for Claude Code.
tools.shown: Browsed the website listing skills, commands and settings.
tools.quote: You kit out Claude code with one install command

tools.name: PostHog
tools.what: Self-hosted product analytics: funnels, retention, session replays, experiments.
tools.shown: Explained uses for a business; no live demo.
tools.quote: PostHog is free, but it's really, really good

tools.name: OpenSEO
tools.what: Open-source SEO tool for keyword research and rank tracking that you run yourself.
tools.shown: Walked through it; founder was on the show before.
tools.quote: open-source SEO that you can run yourself
tools.check: Semrush price claim is the host's.

tools.name: Invoice Ninja
tools.what: Self-hosted quotes, invoices and billing with no per-seat fee.
tools.shown: Explained the quote-to-invoice flow.
tools.quote: why go for a very expensive paid plan from someone else when you could just host this yourself

tools.name: Cal.diy
tools.what: Self-hosted booking page that avoids double-bookings and can take payment first.
tools.shown: Explained the free alternative.
tools.quote: they also put it on GitHub for free for you to use
tools.check: Calendly $12 a seat claimed by host.

tools.name: Autumn
tools.what: Subscriptions and usage or token-based billing for software you build.
tools.shown: Explained pricing options.
tools.quote: This is going to allow you to charge your users.

tools.name: Typebot
tools.what: Self-hosted chat-style forms with branching and lead qualification.
tools.shown: Described what it is.
tools.quote: I don't love how closely their name is to the name Typeform

tools.name: Frappe CRM
tools.what: Customisable open-source CRM for leads and deals.
tools.shown: Compared with Pipedrive; brief.
tools.quote: It's more like a Pipedrive.

tools.name: Mautic
tools.what: Self-hosted email marketing, landing pages and automation.
tools.shown: Described it; said Claude Code can set up follow-up emails.
tools.quote: This is the competitor to GoHighLevel.

tools.name: Chatwoot
tools.what: Self-hosted support inbox with AI replies and no per-seat pricing.
tools.shown: Described it.
tools.quote: you don't have to pay per seat, you can bring your own OpenAI key

tools.name: GrokBot
tools.what: Personal agent with local file access, sub-agents, webhooks and email, run from creators' real workflows.
tools.shown: Played 11 creator clips (meeting notes to agents, file renaming, inbox triage) with commentary.
tools.quote: they can access local files

tools.name: Granola
tools.what: Meeting note-taker whose notes feed GrokBot tasks.
tools.shown: Shown as the source of meeting notes in a creator clip.
tools.quote: he's using Granola as a meeting notetaker

tools.name: Meta Muse
tools.what: Meta's AI agent for bills, price tracking, local files and daily briefs.
tools.shown: Played creator demos and gave verdict.
tools.quote: making Muse free for a huge number of tokens

tools.name: Hyperagent
tools.what: Workspace where humans and several AI agents share Rooms, with permissions and model routing.
tools.shown: Alex demoed Rooms, a paid-ads agent team and permissions.
tools.quote: sign in with Chat GPT and use the subscription you already pay for

tools.name: ChatGPT Dots
tools.what: OpenAI personal agent that can be connected to Slack.
tools.shown: Created a Dot and connected Slack on screen.
tools.quote: what it looks like if I were to use dot directly from them
